# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 93 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 93 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_093_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 9, Chapter 10

**1** "Who are those with the speckled stones that were cast out?" I asked. **2** "These are the double-minded," he said, "who neither live nor are dead. They are of the same nature as those in the cracks of the mountain, but worse: they take oaths and are found to be liars. Therefore they are speckled, because oath-breaking mixed with falsehood has corrupted their faith." **3** "And the short ones?" "These," he said, "are those who believed and were largely upright, but had a measure of malice in them, which is why they are short and not entirely sound. Many of these can be saved if they repent quickly." **4** "And those half-white and half-black?" **5** "These," he said, "are those who are absorbed in business and do not attach themselves to the saints; therefore half of them is living. **6** But since they were much occupied with business and distraction held them, some repented and found salvation; others among them perished utterly — for they held to neither the living nor the dead. These are the double-minded." **7** "Now the white and round stones that did not fit the building — who are they?" I asked. **8** "How long," he said, "will you be foolish and without understanding? These are those who have faith but also have the wealth of this world; when affliction comes, because of their riches and their business they deny their Lord." **9** I said to him, "When then, Lord, will they be fit for the building?" "When," he said, "their riches, which lead their souls astray, are stripped from them. Then they will be of use to God. For just as a round stone cannot become square unless it is cut and something is taken from it, so those who are rich in this world cannot be of use to God unless their riches are cut away from them."

---

*LOGOS: verse 9 contains the Shepherd's most memorable maxim on wealth — riches must be "cut away" before the soul can fit the square tower.*
